summary: The note describes Challenge 21 and Challenge 25, a United Kingdom scheme introduced by the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA) to stop young people obtaining age-restricted products such as cigarettes and alcohol. Under the scheme, retailers ask customers who appear under 21 or 25 to prove their age, even though the legal minimum age to buy alcohol and cigarettes in the UK is 18.
one_line: A UK retail scheme from the British Beer and Pub Association asking apparently under-21 or under-25 customers to prove age when buying restricted goods.
key_facts: Challenge 21 and Challenge 25 are part of a scheme in the United Kingdom.
The scheme was introduced by the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA).
The scheme's intention is to prevent young people gaining access to age restricted products including cigarettes and alcoholic beverages.
Under the scheme, customers attempting to buy age-restricted products are asked to prove their age if, in the retailer's opinion, they look under 21 or 25.
The minimum age to buy alcohol and cigarettes in the UK is 18.
Challenge 21 and Challenge 25 require proof of age even though the legal minimum purchase age in the UK is 18.
